statements.statement:
For an acyclic mixed graph \(G\) on \(n\) vertices and an input cutoff \(d\geq2\), the exact weighted-homogeneous adaptive-ordering algorithm returns ``yes'' whenever \(G\) is rationally identifiable and \(d\geq ID_G\), returns ``no'' whenever \(G\) is not rationally identifiable, and finds lowest-degree identifying formulas.  Its worst-case arithmetic complexity is
\[
 O\!\left(dn^5(3dn)^{4\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}d^2\log(3dn)}\right).
\]

source.locator: Theorem 5.1 and its proof, arXiv:2604.20516v1, together with the formula-output description in Section 5
source.verbatim_statement: If \(G\) is rationally identifiable and \(d\geq\operatorname{ID}_G\), it follows directly from Corollary 4.5 that Algorithm 1 returns ``yes''.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the proof of Theorem 5.1; the theorem's displayed bound and Section 5 output contract support the remaining specialized clauses.

statements.statement:
For every acyclic mixed graph \(G=(V_n,D,B)\), put the formal covariance coordinates \(s\) into a symmetric matrix \(\Sigma\), and interpret \(\omega_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i\neq j\) and \(i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\).  Then
\[
 I_G=\left\langle
 \bigl[(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\bigr]_{ij}-\omega_{ij}:1\leq i\leq j\leq n
 \right\rangle
 \subseteq\mathbb Q[\theta_G,s].
\]
In particular, \(I_G\) has a generating set of total degree at most three.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(R=I_n-\Lambda\).  By acyclicity, after a simultaneous permutation of rows and columns, \(\Lambda\) is strictly triangular.  Hence \(\Lambda^n=0\), \(\det R=1\), and
\[
 T:=R^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}
\]
has entries in \(\mathbb Q[\theta_G]\).  Let \(J\) denote the displayed ideal, with each structurally absent off-diagonal entry of \(\Omega\) set equal to zero as required by \(\mathrm{ass:omega\mbox{-}support}\).  In the quotient by \(J\), the defining relations are
\[
 R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R=\Omega.
\]
Multiplication on the left by \(T^{\mathsf T}\) and on the right by \(T\) is valid over the polynomial ring and gives
\[
 \Sigma=T^{\mathsf T}\Omega T.
\]
Consequently the homomorphism
\[
 \mathbb Q[\theta_G,s]/J\longrightarrow\mathbb Q[\theta_G]
\]
which fixes \(\theta_G\) and sends \(s\) to \(\phi_G(\theta_G)\) is an isomorphism: its inverse sends every source coordinate to its residue class, and the last display shows that every covariance residue class is the prescribed polynomial in those source coordinates.  Its kernel before quotienting is therefore exactly \(J\).  By the definition \(I_G=\ker\tau_G\), this proves \(I_G=J\).

Each entry of \(R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R-\Omega\) is a sum of terms of the forms \(\sigma_{ij}\), \(\lambda_{ab}\sigma_{ij}\), \(\lambda_{ab}\sigma_{ij}\lambda_{cd}\), and \(\omega_{ij}\).  Their total degrees are at most three, proving the final assertion.

statements.statement:
Let \(n\geq1\).  An ideal over a field in at most \(n(n+1)\) indeterminates, generated by polynomials of total degree at most three, has for every admissible monomial order a reduced Gr\"obner basis whose elements have total degree at most
\[
 2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{n(n+1)-1}}<U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}.
\]

source.locator: Corollary 8.3, specialized to degree three and at most n(n+1) variables
source.verbatim_statement: Let F be a subset of K[X], I the ideal generated by F, and let d be the maximum degree of any f in F. Then for any admissible ordering, the degree of polynomials required in a Groebner basis for I is bounded by 2((d^2/2)+d)^(2^(n-1)).

attestation.note: Verified against Dubé 1990, Corollary 8.3, in the SIAM publisher record and the complete author-hosted PDF at University of Waterloo; the run statement substitutes d=3 and r at most n(n+1), then applies the elementary displayed comparison to U_2(n).

statements.statement:
For every \(n\geq1\) and every \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\),
\[
 ID_G\leq U_2(n).
\]
More precisely, \(\mathfrak B(G)\leq U_2(n)\); every structural coordinate \(q\in\theta_G\) has a direct certificate \(q a_q(s)-b_q(s)\in I_G\) with \(\tau_G(a_q)\neq0\) and degree at most \(\mathfrak B(G)\), and, after the structural coordinates have entered \(S\), every supported disturbance coordinate has the denominator-one certificate
\[
 q-\bigl[(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\bigr]_{ij}\in I_G
\]
of degree at most three.  Consequently \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)\).  For \(n\geq2\),
\[
 U_2(n)=
 \left\lfloor
 2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{n(n+1)/2+2n-4}}
 \right\rfloor,
\]
while \(U_2(1)=15\).
statements.justification: Eliminating supported disturbance coordinates gives a graph-sensitive structural cutoff, and the indegree-two edge count converts it into a sharper unconditional graph-uniform bound.
statements.gap: The elimination cutoffs are not asserted to be sharp; direct cutoff-degree certificates are proved for structural coordinates, while disturbance coordinates are recovered recursively at degree three.
statements.consumer: Both the graph-sensitive and graph-independent exact stopping schedules use this bound.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\), its directed part is acyclic, its maximum directed indegree is at most two, and \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image.  Therefore \(\mathrm{thm:graph\mbox{-}sensitive\mbox{-}elimination\mbox{-}bound}\) supplies the stated direct structural certificates, the subsequent degree-three disturbance certificates, and
\[
 ID_G\leq\mathfrak B(G).
 \tag{1}
\]

It remains to compare the graph-sensitive cutoff to a function of \(n\) alone.  If \(n=1\), acyclicity forces \(|D|=0\), so
\[
 \mathfrak B(G)
 =\left\lfloor2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{1-1}}\right\rfloor
 =15
 =U_2(1).
 \tag{2}
\]
Suppose \(n\geq2\).  A finite directed acyclic graph has a vertex of indegree zero: otherwise, repeatedly choosing a parent must revisit a vertex and create a directed cycle.  Removing such a vertex preserves acyclicity, so induction on the number of vertices produces a topological ordering \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\).  Every parent of \(v_j\) belongs to \(\{v_1,\ldots,v_{j-1}\}\).  The first vertex therefore has indegree zero, the second has indegree at most one, and each later vertex has indegree at most two by \(\mathrm{ass:indegree\mbox{-}two}\).  Summing indegrees yields
\[
 |D|=\sum_{j=1}^n|\operatorname{pa}_G(v_j)|
 \leq0+1+2(n-2)=2n-3.
 \tag{3}
\]
The map \(x\mapsto\left\lfloor2(15/2)^{2^x}\right\rfloor\) is increasing.  With \(m=n(n+1)/2\), (3) gives
\[
 \mathfrak B(G)
 =\left\lfloor2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{m+|D|-1}}\right\rfloor
 \leq
 \left\lfloor2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{m+2n-4}}\right\rfloor
 =U_2(n).
 \tag{4}
\]
Combining (1), (2), and (4) proves \(ID_G\leq U_2(n)\) and all of the more precise certificate claims.  Finally, \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\) is a finite set of mixed graphs on \(V_n\), so maximizing the proved inequality over its members and using the definition of \(D_2(n)\) gives
\[
 D_2(n)=\max_{G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)}ID_G\leq U_2(n).
\]
No lower-bound or sharpness assertion is used.

statements.statement:
The six-vertex graph \(K_6\) is generically rationally identifiable, belongs to \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(6)\), and satisfies
\[
 ID_{K_6}\leq7.
\]
No matching degree-seven lower bound and no auxiliary-cutset failure claim is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\sigma_{ab}=\Sigma_{ab}\) and
\[
 x_i=\lambda_{i,i+1},\qquad 1\leq i\leq5.
\]
The directed part of \(K_6\) is a chain, so it is acyclic and has maximum indegree one.  For coefficient indices \(1\leq i<j\leq5\) such that the disturbance pair \(\{i+1,j+1\}\) is missing, the corresponding entry of
\(\Omega=(I_6-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_6-\Lambda)\) is
\[
 E_{ij}(x_i,x_j)
 =\sigma_{ij}x_ix_j-\sigma_{i,j+1}x_i-\sigma_{i+1,j}x_j+\sigma_{i+1,j+1}=0. \tag{7}
\]
This identity follows from the covariance parametrization and the support restriction \(\mathrm{ass:omega\mbox{-}support}\); it is a cubic graph-ideal relation.

Choose the shared coefficient
\[
 t=x_3.
\]
For \(k=1,2\), define the covariance-linear polynomials
\[
 D_k(t)=\sigma_{k3}t-\sigma_{k4},\qquad
 N_k(t)=\sigma_{k+1,3}t-\sigma_{k+1,4}.
\]
Then (7) for the missing pairs indexed by \((1,3)\) and \((2,3)\) gives
\[
 D_k(t)x_k-N_k(t)=0,\qquad k=1,2. \tag{8}
\]
For \(k=4,5\), define
\[
 D_k(t)=\sigma_{3k}t-\sigma_{4k},\qquad
 N_k(t)=\sigma_{3,k+1}t-\sigma_{4,k+1}.
\]
The missing pairs indexed by \((3,4)\) and \((3,5)\) similarly give
\[
 D_k(t)x_k-N_k(t)=0,\qquad k=4,5. \tag{9}
\]

Use the remaining missing pair in each triangle to define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H(t)&=D_1(t)D_2(t)E_{12}\!\left(\frac{N_1(t)}{D_1(t)},\frac{N_2(t)}{D_2(t)}\right),\\
 J(t)&=D_4(t)D_5(t)E_{45}\!\left(\frac{N_4(t)}{D_4(t)},\frac{N_5(t)}{D_5(t)}\right).
 \end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
The products in (10) mean the polynomials obtained after clearing the displayed denominators.  Every summand is one covariance coordinate times a product of two covariance-linear polynomials.  Thus
\[
 H(t)=h_2t^2+h_1t+h_0,\qquad
 J(t)=j_2t^2+j_1t+j_0, \tag{11}
\]
where every \(h_j,j_j\in\mathbb Q[s]\) has covariance degree at most three.  Equations (7)--(9), without division, imply \(H(x_3)=J(x_3)=0\) after substitution by \(\tau_{K_6}\).  Consequently
\[
 j_2H(t)-h_2J(t)
 =\Delta(s)t-N(s), \tag{12}
\]
where
\[
 \Delta=j_2h_1-h_2j_1,\qquad
 N=h_2j_0-j_2h_0,\qquad
 \deg_s\Delta,\deg_sN\leq6. \tag{13}
\]
It remains to verify the denominator condition rather than assume it.

Take \(x_i=i/(i+1)\), give \(\Omega\) unit diagonal, give every allowed off-diagonal entry the value \(1/100\), and keep the six graphically missing entries equal to zero.  For every nonzero \(v\in\mathbb R^6\), the inequality \(2|v_iv_j|\leq v_i^2+v_j^2\) gives
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}\Omega v
 \geq \sum_{i=1}^6v_i^2-
 \frac1{100}\sum_{i<j}(v_i^2+v_j^2)
 \geq\frac{95}{100}\sum_{i=1}^6v_i^2>0.
\]
Thus \(\Omega\succ0\), so this is a legal parameter point.  At this point, exact multiplication of \(\Sigma=(I_6-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_6-\Lambda)^{-1}\) gives
\[
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}
 1&51/100&7/20&109/400&57/250&1/5\\
 51/100&63/50&169/200&511/800&263/500&34/75\\
 7/20&169/200&47/30&707/600&361/375&37/45\\
 109/400&511/800&707/600&1509/800&381/250&257/200\\
 57/250&263/500&361/375&381/250&2789/1250&2807/1500\\
 1/5&34/75&37/45&257/200&2807/1500&185/72
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Substitution of these entries into (10) gives, up to nonzero rational scalar factors,
\[
 H(t)=(4t-3)(940t-1309),\qquad
 J(t)=(4t-3)(705860t-1145331). \tag{14}
\]
The second roots \(1309/940\) and \(1145331/705860\) are distinct, so the coefficient \(\Delta\) in the leading-term cancellation (12) is nonzero at this legal point.  At the true value \(t=3/4\), the four propagation denominators in (8)--(9) evaluate respectively to
\[
 -\frac1{100},\quad-\frac1{200},\quad-\frac{401}{400},\quad-\frac{401}{500}, \tag{15}
\]
and hence are nonzero as well.  Thus \(\tau_{K_6}(\Delta)\) and each \(\tau_{K_6}(D_k(x_3))\) are nonzero polynomials on the model.  Positivity is used here only to ensure that the nonvanishing witness belongs to the admissible covariance model; a polynomial nonzero at one such point is generically nonzero.

Equations (12)--(13) now give the valid first recursive certificate
\[
 x_3\Delta(s)-N(s)\in I_{K_6},\qquad
 \deg\{x_3\Delta-N\}\leq7, \tag{16}
\]
with a denominator nonzero on the model.  After adjoining \(x_3\), equations (8)--(9) identify \(x_1,x_2,x_4,x_5\).  Each has total certificate degree at most three, since its highest-degree term is \(x_k\sigma_{ab}x_3\), and (15) verifies that its denominator is not the zero polynomial.  Finally, for every free disturbance coordinate,
\[
 \omega_{ab}-\bigl[(I_6-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_6-\Lambda)\bigr]_{ab}=0 \tag{17}
\]
is a degree-at-most-three certificate with denominator one after the structural coefficients have been adjoined.  Hence the displayed order identifies every coordinate of \(\theta_{K_6}\) with maximum degree seven, proving \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\).

The same formulas give a rational inverse to \(\phi_{K_6}\) on the nonempty Zariski-open set where \(\Delta\prod_{k\in\{1,2,4,5\}}D_k(x_3)\neq0\).  Therefore \(\phi_{K_6}\) is generically birational onto its image.  Together with acyclicity and indegree one, this proves \(K_6\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(6)\).  The proof supplies no lower bound beyond what an exact closure computation may later establish.
statements.justification: The shared central coefficient makes both triangle constraints quadratic with covariance-degree-three coefficients, improving the audited rational upper bound to seven.
statements.gap: Only the upper bound is established; exact minimum degree requires the separate filtered-elimination artifact.
statements.consumer: The exact six-vertex calibration is reduced to closure computations at degrees below seven.

statements.statement:
Let \(k_{\mathrm{alg}}\geq 1\).  If an ideal over a field in \(k_{\mathrm{alg}}\) indeterminates is generated by polynomials of total degree at most three, then, for every admissible monomial order, every element of its reduced Gr\"obner basis has total degree at most
\[
 \left\lfloor
 2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{k_{\mathrm{alg}}-1}}
 \right\rfloor.
\]

source.locator: Corollary 8.3, specialized to generating degree three
source.verbatim_statement: Let F be a subset of K[X], I the ideal generated by F, and let d be the maximum degree of any f in F. Then for any admissible ordering, the degree of polynomials required in a Groebner basis for I is bounded by 2((d^2/2)+d)^(2^(n-1)).

attestation.note: Verified against Dubé 1990, Corollary 8.3, in the SIAM publisher record and the complete author-hosted PDF at University of Waterloo; substituting d=3 yields the cited general cubic bound, with the floor harmless because basis degrees are integers.

statements.statement:
Let \(G=(V_n,D,B)\) be an acyclic mixed graph for which \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image.  For every structural coordinate \(q=\lambda_{uv}\in\theta_G\), there are \(a_q,b_q\in\mathbb Q[s]\) such that
\[
 \tau_G(a_q)\neq0,
 \qquad
 q a_q(s)-b_q(s)\in I_G,
 \qquad
 \deg\{q a_q-b_q\}\leq\mathfrak B(G).
\]
After all structural coordinates have been identified, every supported disturbance coordinate \(q=\omega_{ij}\in\theta_G\) has the recursive certificate
\[
 q-\bigl[(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\bigr]_{ij}\in I_G
\]
of total degree at most three and denominator one.  Consequently \(ID_G\leq\mathfrak B(G)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(m=n(n+1)/2\), \(e=|D|\), and let \(L\) be the set of the \(e\) structural coordinates \(\lambda_{uv}\).  Put
\[
 R=\mathbb Q[L,s],
 \qquad
 T=R[\omega_{ij}:i=j\text{ or }i\leftrightarrow j\in B],
 \qquad
 H=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda).
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(R\) has exactly \(m+e\) indeterminates.  Let
\[
 \mathcal M=\lbrace(i,j):1\leq i<j\leq n,\ i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\rbrace,
 \qquad
 \mathcal E=\lbrace(i,j):1\leq i\leq j\leq n,\ i=j\text{ or }i\leftrightarrow j\in B\rbrace.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:cubic\mbox{-}graph\mbox{-}ideal\mbox{-}presentation}\) and the support restriction \(\mathrm{ass:omega\mbox{-}support}\),
\[
 I_G=
 \langle H_{ij}:(i,j)\in\mathcal M\rangle_T
 +\langle H_{ij}-\omega_{ij}:(i,j)\in\mathcal E\rangle_T.
 \tag{2}
\]

Define the \(R\)-algebra homomorphism \(\pi:T\to R\) by
\[
 \pi(\omega_{ij})=H_{ij}\quad ((i,j)\in\mathcal E),
 \qquad
 \pi|_R=\operatorname{id}_R.
\]
Successively viewing \(T\) as a univariate polynomial ring in each supported \(\omega_{ij}\) and dividing by the monic polynomial \(\omega_{ij}-H_{ij}\) proves
\[
 \ker(\pi)=\langle H_{ij}-\omega_{ij}:(i,j)\in\mathcal E\rangle_T.
 \tag{3}
\]
If \(f\in I_G\cap R\), then (2), followed by \(\pi\), gives
\[
 f=\pi(f)\in\langle H_{ij}:(i,j)\in\mathcal M\rangle_R.
\]
The reverse inclusion follows directly from (2).  Hence the structural elimination ideal is
\[
 J_G:=I_G\cap R=\langle H_{ij}:(i,j)\in\mathcal M\rangle_R.
 \tag{4}
\]
Every entry of \(H\) has total degree at most three in \((L,s)\), since it is an entry of the product of a matrix linear in \(L\), a matrix linear in \(s\), and another matrix linear in \(L\).  Thus (4) is a degree-three presentation in \(m+e\) variables.

Fix a structural coordinate \(q\in L\), and choose the lexicographic order in which the coordinates in \(L\setminus\{q\}\) precede \(q\), which precedes every covariance coordinate.  By \(\mathrm{lem:dube\mbox{-}general\mbox{-}cubic\mbox{-}degree\mbox{-}bound}\), every member of the reduced Gr\"obner basis \(\mathcal B_q\) of \(J_G\) has degree at most
\[
 \mathfrak B(G)=
 \left\lfloor2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{m+e-1}}\right\rfloor.
 \tag{5}
\]
Set
\[
 K=J_G\cap\mathbb Q[s],
 \quad
 J_q=J_G\cap\mathbb Q[q,s],
 \quad
 \mathcal H_q=\mathcal B_q\cap\mathbb Q[q,s],
 \quad
 \mathcal H_0=\mathcal B_q\cap\mathbb Q[s].
 \tag{6}
\]
We verify the elimination fact used below.  If \(f\in J_q\), some \(g\in\mathcal B_q\) has leading monomial dividing the leading monomial of \(f\).  That leading monomial contains no coordinate in \(L\setminus\{q\}\).  Under the chosen lexicographic order, any term of \(g\) containing such a coordinate would exceed every term containing none, so \(g\in\mathbb Q[q,s]\).  Therefore \(\mathcal H_q\) is a Gr\"obner basis of \(J_q\).  Applying the same argument after eliminating \(q\) shows that \(\mathcal H_0\) is a Gr\"obner basis of \(K\).

The ideal \(J_G\) is the kernel of the restriction of \(\tau_G\) to \(R\), by the definition \(I_G=\ker(\tau_G)\) and (4).  It is therefore prime, and
\[
 A:=\mathbb Q[s]/K
\]
is a domain embedded by covariance substitution in \(\mathbb Q[\theta_G]\).  Generic birationality of \(\phi_G\) says that the function field generated by the covariance coordinates equals \(\mathbb Q(\theta_G)\).  In particular, the image of \(q\) lies in \(\operatorname{Frac}(A)\).  Consequently there are \(a,b\in\mathbb Q[s]\) with
\[
 a\notin K,
 \qquad
 qa-b\in J_q.
 \tag{7}
\]
Replace \(a\) and \(b\) by their normal forms \(a'\) and \(b'\) modulo \(\mathcal H_0\).  Since \(a-a'\in K\subseteq J_G\) and \(b-b'\in K\subseteq J_G\), the ideal property gives
\[
 f':=qa'-b'\in J_q.
 \tag{8}
\]
Moreover \(a'\neq0\), because \(a\notin K\), and \(a'\) is reduced with respect to \(\mathcal H_0\).

Reduce the nonzero polynomial \(f'\) to zero by \(\mathcal H_q\).  Its leading monomial contains \(q\), because \(q\) precedes all covariance variables and \(a'\neq0\).  No leading monomial from \(\mathcal H_0\) divides a monomial of \(qa'\), since that would make the corresponding monomial of \(a'\) reducible.  Hence some \(h_q\in\mathcal H_q\setminus\mathcal H_0\) has a leading monomial containing exactly one power of \(q\) and dividing a monomial of \(qa'\).  No term of \(h_q\) can contain a higher power of \(q\), because such a term would precede its leading monomial.  Thus
\[
 h_q=q a_q(s)-b_q(s)
 \tag{9}
\]
for some nonzero \(a_q,b_q\in\mathbb Q[s]\), after changing a sign if necessary.  If \(a_q\in K\), then the leading monomial of \(a_q\) is divisible by the leading monomial of an element of \(\mathcal H_0\).  The corresponding monomial of \(q a_q\) is a monomial of \(h_q\), contradicting reducedness of \(\mathcal B_q\).  Therefore
\[
 a_q\notin K,
 \qquad
 \tau_G(a_q)\neq0.
 \tag{10}
\]
Equations (5), (9), and (10) prove the claimed direct structural certificate.

It remains to identify the supported disturbance coordinates without increasing the largest recursive degree.  Once all coordinates in \(L\) have entered the identified set, equation (2) supplies, for every \((i,j)\in\mathcal E\),
\[
 \omega_{ij}-H_{ij}\in I_G.
 \tag{11}
\]
This is a recursive certificate with denominator one, which is nonzero everywhere, and its total degree is at most three by the degree calculation following (4).  Finally, \(m+e\geq1\), so (5) gives \(\mathfrak B(G)\geq15>3\).  Ordering the structural certificates (9) first and the disturbance certificates (11) afterward therefore gives
\[
 ID_G\leq\max\{\mathfrak B(G),3\}=\mathfrak B(G),
\]
by \(\mathrm{def:recursive\mbox{-}certificate}\).

statements.statement:
Let \(G\) be any acyclic mixed graph on \(n\) vertices.  One exact call to \(\operatorname{DBI}(G,\mathfrak B(G))\), with no wall-clock timeout, terminates and returns ``yes'' with minimum-degree rational formulas if and only if \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image.  Its arithmetic complexity is
\[
 O\!\left(
 \mathfrak B(G)n^5
 \{3\mathfrak B(G)n\}^{4\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathfrak B(G)^2\log(3\mathfrak B(G)n)}
 \right).
\]
A ``no'' answer is accompanied by a complete exact bounded-search certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(\mathfrak B(G)\geq15\), it is an admissible cutoff for \(\mathrm{lem:dbi\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}cutoff\mbox{-}guarantee}\).  If \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image, \(\mathrm{thm:graph\mbox{-}sensitive\mbox{-}elimination\mbox{-}bound}\) gives
\[
 ID_G\leq\mathfrak B(G),
 \tag{1}
\]
so the exact algorithm returns ``yes'' and its adaptive internal ordering returns formulas at the least successful recursive degree.  If \(\phi_G\) is not generically birational onto its image, the fixed-cutoff guarantee returns ``no''.  This proves the equivalence.

The cutoff \(\mathfrak B(G)\) is finite.  At a fixed finite cutoff the algorithm has finitely many monomials, recursive states, and exact row reductions; removing the wall-clock timeout therefore yields termination.  Substituting \(d=\mathfrak B(G)\) in the complexity bound of \(\mathrm{lem:dbi\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}cutoff\mbox{-}guarantee}\) gives the displayed arithmetic bound.

For a ``no'' output, retain the terminal exact rank-intersection transcript.  If \(S\) is its terminal identified set, then \(S\subsetneq\theta_G\), and for every \(q\in\theta_G\setminus S\) it records
\[
 \dim A_{\mathfrak B(G)}(S)
 +\dim\bigl(qC_{\mathfrak B(G)}(S)\bigr)
 =\dim\bigl(A_{\mathfrak B(G)}(S)+qC_{\mathfrak B(G)}(S)\bigr).
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus all relevant intersections are zero and \(S\) is a proper fixed point of the degree closure.  By \(\mathrm{thm:closure\mbox{-}characterization}\), (2) certifies \(ID_G>\mathfrak B(G)\).  In view of (1), this is impossible under generic birationality.  Hence the finite rational transcript is a complete nonidentifiability certificate, not a timeout status.
statements.justification: The actual edge count yields a smaller unconditional formula-producing cutoff for each input graph.
statements.gap: The cutoff is an elimination guarantee rather than a claim about the sharp recursive degree.
statements.consumer: Users may run the exact identification algorithm at the graph-sensitive cutoff instead of the larger graph-independent cutoff.
